diagnostic_interpretation.balance: Balanced four-worker work is evenly partitioned; hot ownership concentrates work. Reported worker waits are summed across workers and overlap coordinator work.
diagnostic_interpretation.coordinator: Coordinator pipeline thread CPU is about 145-147ms against about 147-153ms uninstrumented pipeline wall time; this supports a coordinator bottleneck here, without isolating decode/global checks/read costs.
diagnostic_interpretation.failed_hypotheses: Descriptive comparisons; no directional statistical hypothesis or test was preregistered.
diagnostic_interpretation.instrumentation: Detailed per-event timestamps substantially increase measured worker CPU; use the plain arms for total-time comparisons and treat stage figures as instrumented observations.
rejected_proposals: An unconditional vector-to-tree ladder replacement: tree is slower in five of six current-host cases, although it wins for 4096 uniformly changed levels.

Remove the direct reference window without losing mixed-operation index throughput: hash-only kernels take about 5.26x as long on recent references and 4.57x on retained-old references in these traces.
Add workers to accelerate this bounded pipeline: two/four workers do not beat one worker in the observed medians.
diagnostic_interpretation.scaling: One worker has the lowest median total time for both synthetic inputs; adding workers does not improve these observed bounded replays.
diagnostic_interpretation.scope: Comparisons apply to these fixed inputs and active-host conditions; no general superiority or dedicated-host service-level claim.

engine_mode_boundaries: Throughput sums fresh-subject command kernels; latency includes per-command timestamps/classification; batch distributions are means, not individual tails. Warmup executes but its timing is not exported by the original harness. Setup/reset, independent checks and reporting are outside the throughput kernel.
limitations: Current-host measurements on an active development machine; every repetition retained; original strict CPU/pageout gate failures remain recorded.
Synthetic traces do not establish real-market workload behavior.
Fixed arm order, three pipeline/five structure repetitions, OS scheduling, heterogeneous cores and background load limit inference.
No hard CPU affinity, frequency isolation, certified cache state or hardware PMU measurements.
Stage instrumentation changes work; overlapping wall/CPU/wait measures must not be added as exclusive fractions.
Replay comparisons cover only the two bounded synthetic inputs and 1/2/4 workers; they do not establish full-day or different-partition scaling.
Linux TSan file-limit BUS remains unresolved; historical empirical findings unchanged.
